verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. (1) The proposal's 'file browser starts at your home folder' is only true for per-user installs: launch_jupyter.py lines 208-214 set root_dir=home only if the Welcome notebook sits under home, else the install prefix (all-users installs). (2) 'Right-click > Download' is wrong advice for a server that runs on the user's own machine, because the files are already local. (3) A generic page cannot say where an app's results land or what the output looks like, and 'result about 15 minutes after install' cannot be promised without example data (see A2). (4) A numbered walkthrough that names real button labels from one reference app, written without a clean run, would be invented UI text.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do not rewrite using-apps.md into a full walkthrough. Make three small edits, all in LabConstrictor-Site (hand-written, so single-source is respected). (a) content/guides/using-apps.md: delete the duplicated 'Open it' list (it repeats notebook_usage.md sections 1-2) and link to the notebook usage guide. Say what is true: the Welcome notebook shows its table of notebooks only after you run its first cell (the shipped Welcome.ipynb has 0 outputs; notebook_usage section 4 already says 'Once you run the welcome notebook'). (b) Add a short 'Where your files are' section, worded only from the code: JupyterLab runs on your own computer; for a normal per-user install its file browser starts at your home folder, otherwise at the app's install folder. Say that where results are written is shown in the app's notebook, and link to the app page's 'Using it' (the app's own example, see A2). Leave out 'Download' and Explorer/Finder steps. (c) data/hubs.yaml card 'Open it and work': change 'a Welcome notebook that lists its notebooks' to say you run its first cell to list them. Keep the slug. Put the first-success check and the expected output in the app repos' own examples (A2), not here. If the title changes, add a data/redirects.yaml line.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. The idea of a Verified badge meaning 'a maintainer ran the documented example' redefines policy in content/submit.md line 49 (now: 'a maintainer also installed and ran a specific version'), and no app has such an example yet. A site-wide build warning for featured apps without quickstart/docs_url fires on all 3 featured apps every day, and scheduled builds open issues, so it would produce standing noise about repos the team does not own. Asking the initialiser form to prompt for a quickstart is more machinery than a 6-app catalogue needs. Several of the auditor's details are fine to cite but should be re-checked by the app owners (e.g. the 'Use test dataset' checkbox label and 'up to 10 min download' are unverified by me).
verdicts.refined_proposal: Work in the app repos, one app at a time, and change nothing in the site code. (1) CellMigrationLab/CellTracksColab (first): add a `quickstart` (<=6 plain-text steps) and `docs_url` to its labconstrictor-app.yaml, and a short README 'Try it with test data' section (the notebooks already use Zenodo records 8413510 / 8420011, and a Results folder; state what files appear). The site already renders `quickstart` as an ordered list in 'Using it' (pages_apps.py using_section), so the app page gains the example with no site change. (2) CellMigrationLab/NucleiSky: fix the NucleiSky-test URLs in .tools/docs/download_executable.md lines 13, 51, 111 and the other release links to the real repo (confirm first whether the app's workflow regenerates that file from the template), and give one small example (data link, which notebook, expected output); it already has docs/2D/data_preparation.md to link from `docs_url`. (3) VLab4Mic only if its authors want to. In the template, edit .tools/docs/app_manifest.md line 31 to name 'quick start' as the field that makes the page useful. Skip: the build warning (at most a non-issue note in build/problems.md if the team really wants one), the initialiser change, and the Verified redefinition (a team policy decision, to be taken separately).

verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium to high if written as proposed. Admin rights, disk space, supported OS versions and the macOS install location are unverified (the auditor says so), so stating them would invent facts. 'Intel Macs not supported' is one app's statement (Playground README); the generic guide is right to offer an Intel installer because NucleiSky ships MacOSX-x86_64 packages, so the guide must not say it generally.
verdicts.refined_proposal: In the template (CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor, .tools/docs/install.md) add only claims backed by code or already in the docs. 'Before you start': an internet connection is needed while installing, because post_install.bat/.sh run `pip install -r requirements`; the installer sizes and the systems and architectures each app offers are listed on the app's page in the App Centre (so no OS version list here). 'Check that it worked' once, before 'Next': a terminal window opens, then your browser opens JupyterLab with the Welcome notebook; this can take a little while the first time (wording taken from notebook_usage.md section 2). Add one link to the troubleshooting guide next to it. Omit admin rights, disk space and the macOS location until someone tests a clean install. Fix the pager mismatch on the site, not in the template: reorder data/guides.yaml so the pager (which follows that order) agrees with install.md's 'Next' text. For example, put notebook_usage.md directly after install.md and the site-owned using-apps page after it. The template keeps pointing to notebook_usage.md, which is correct in the template's own order.
